subject: POC Load Probes: clarifications + short-term milestones
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <pri.rao@vectormetrics.com>, ops+trial@vectormetrics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: POC Load Probes: clarifications + short-term milestones

Hi Priyanka — great to meet with you and the VM team earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying probes so we can finalize the POC plan and trial windows. Please confirm the items below where possible by end of day tomorrow.

Summary of ask from the call:
- Objective: validate 95th-pct latency and cost at expected traffic for search-similarity API during peak and sustain.
- Acceptance target (requested by product): 95th-pct generation latency <= 200ms for single-tenant (hosted) configuration, and token-cost target < $0.00035/token.

Traffic profile (from call notes) — please confirm/correct:
- Steady-state RPS: 180 RPS (search embedding + short text generation mix)
- Peak bursts: up to 1,200 RPS for ~5-10 minute windows, 3x/day (morning, lunch, evening)
- Concurrency: 400 concurrent connections at peak windows
- Token distribution: median request ~45 tokens, 90th pct ~380 tokens (due to some long debug dumps)

Clarifying probes (we need answers to design the workload probes):
1) Do you expect repeated identical prefixes that would benefit from prefix/KV cache (e.g., same query + different user metadata)?
2) Are there hard per-request token upper bounds we should enforce in the test harness?
3) Will the trial use real production payloads or scrubbed/sampled traces? If scrubbed, can you provide a ~1-hour sample (we can accept JSONL) — that'll let us simulate realistic token/chunk distributions.

Proposed short-term milestones:
- Today+tomorrow: VM provides confirmation on the three probes + sample payload (attachment recommended).
- Within 3 business days: Redwood runs small-shaped probe (10m ramp to 200 RPS) and shares initial latency/cost snapshot.
- Within 7 business days: Full trial run with two 10-minute bursts at target peak and 30-minute sustain at steady-state.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood SRE/ops: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com) — trial infra + runbook
- Redwood Success criteria owner: Soojin Lee (soojin_lee@redwood.com) — acceptance gating and report
- VectorMetrics: Priyanka Rao (trial coordination + sample payloads)

Attachments: I requested a sample payload + a one-page POC scope sheet — please attach if you can (we can accept JSONL or zipped JSONL).

If anything above looks off, flag it inline. Otherwise we'll take the probes as the input for a detailed runbook and timeline.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment stubs referenced: vectormetrics_sample_payloads.json (JSONL, 12MB), poc_scope_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Priyanka Rao <pri.rao@vectormetrics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+trial@vectormetrics.com
Date: 2026-09-19T12:37:00-04:00
Subject: Re: POC Load Probes: clarifications + short-term milestones

Thanks Diego — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below and attaching the sanitized sample payloads (vectormetrics_sample_payloads.json).

Answers to probes:
1) Prefix/cache: Yes — ~60% of queries share a stable search prefix; cache should show benefit. Some requests append user-specific metadata (~40%) so KV reuse is partial.
2) Hard token caps: We have a business rule to truncate at 1024 tokens for generation requests; similarity embeddings are usually under 256 tokens.
3) Payloads: attaching a 1-hour trimmed trace (sanitized) — this is what we want simulated. There are two payload shapes: "short-query" (~75% of traffic, median 35 tokens) and "session-dump" (~10% of traffic, bursts of long token lengths up to 800).

Extra notes:
- Peak bursts are driven by scheduled batch jobs that fan out vanity queries; they happen roughly at 07:30, 12:30, 18:00 local PT.
- Ops team requests that we include a failure-injection step (simulate a Redis cache miss spike) during one of the probe runs to see recovery behavior.

We'll confirm the exact files again after you validate they load in your harness.

— Priyanka
Priyanka Rao
Head of Platform Reliability, VectorMetrics
pri.rao@vectormetrics.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-20T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Load Probes: clarifications + short-term milestones

Thanks Priyanka — sample payload received and looks good at a glance. Next steps:

1) Ben, can you pick an initial probe window tomorrow morning (09:00-10:00 PT) and run a 30-minute steady-state at 200 RPS followed by two 10-minute bursts at 1,000 RPS to validate control paths? Please include one failure-injection (cache miss) during the second burst.
2) Soojin, please draft the acceptance checklist: perf targets, cost targets, and rollback criteria. I'll share with Priyanka so they can confirm alignment.
3) Priyanka, we'll share the runbook link and a short script to replay the JSONL file against our harness — expect a Drive link and a short README in the next 4 hours.

I'll log these milestones in HS-0008473 and follow up after the morning probe.

Diego
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Rao <pri.rao@vectormetrics.com>, ops+trial@vectormetrics.com
Date: 2026-09-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Load Probes: clarifications + short-term milestones

Planned runbook (brief):
- Prep (1 hour): stage a test cluster with same model variant + quantization profile suggested by RDW research. Load the provided JSONL and sanity-check tokenization stats.
- Probe A (09:00 PT): 30m sustain @ 200 RPS — capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, token output counts, GPU utilization, and cost-per-token estimate.
- Probe B (09:40 PT): two bursts — 10m @ 1,000 RPS each, inject Redis miss during second burst, verify fallback latency and error rates.

Questions for Priyanka (quick):
- For the cache-miss injection, do you want us to simulate cold-key miss only (random 5% of prefixes) or a full eviction (simulate 100% miss for 30s)? Either has different operational implications.
- Confirm whether session-dump requests (the long ones) should be treated as individual requests or split into chunked streams in the harness. Splitting will change concurrency semantics.

I'll kick off infra prep once we get your answers; expected runtime for the whole probe run is ~3 hours including setup and teardown. I'll attach a link to the raw logs and an initial dashboard snapshot when complete.

— Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
